newsitem.title: JAPAN: TIFFE Euroyen end higher ahead of U.S. jobs data.
newsitem.headline: TIFFE Euroyen end higher ahead of U.S. jobs data.

text.p: Key December three-month euroyen interest rate futures settled firmer on Friday on position squaring ahead of key U.S. employment data due later on Friday.

One city bank dealer said the contract was lifted by technically driven short-covering, although some traders said gains in the late afternoon were due to a report that a senior Japanese banker said he did not think the Bank of Japan (BOJ) was ready to raise interest rates.

The Jiji news agency quoted Naotaka Saeki, chairman of the Federation of Bankers Associations of Japan, as telling a parliamentary committee meeting that it seems the BOJ does not think the situation calls for raising interest rates, judging from economic conditions.

"Some people talked about the report as a reason to buy, but the late buying was seen as largely technical," said a dealer at a brokerage house. December settled up 0.03 at 98.88 after moving from 98.85 to 98.89. Turnover was 35,522 lots.
December Euroyen stayed inside the recent 98.80-98.90 range on Friday and are likely to do so next week, the dealer said.

Some dealers, however, said a large lot of late buying came from U.S. hedge funds. U.S. hedge funds continued to cover short positions in the night session, which started at 3.30 p.m. (0630 GMT), they said.
In the cash market, interest rates firmed in part because Dai-Ichi Kangyo Bank Ltd (DKB) was actively raising long-term funds, traders said.

Some traders said one-month certificates of deposit (CD) were issued at 0.57 and 0.58 percent, up from the last issued rate of 0.56. City banks other than DKB also issued one-month CDs at 0.58 percent in small volumes, they said.

In addition, DKB was said to have raised funds through one-month euroyen at 0.58 and 0.59 percent, compared with Thursday's 0.58 percent, they said. A DKB trader declined to comment on the talk of the transactions.
Prosecutors on Thursday arrested four DKB officials on suspicion of violating Japan's Commercial Code by making illegal loans worth 11.78 billion yen to a racketeer.
In the interbank market, the key overnight call rate was traded mainly at 0.49 percent, up from Thursday's 0.48 percent.
The BOJ's morning operation was less accommodative than in previous days, but it was in line with market expectations.
The BOJ's injection of 300 billion yen on Friday resulted in a market surplus of some 100 billion yen for the day.
The BOJ left a market surplus of some 200 billion yen on Wednesday and Thursday to help meet banks' demand for funds for tax payments. -- Risa Maeda, Tokyo Treasury Desk +81-3-3432-8570
